Based on a few things that I've explained before in the past, and small hints by Christopher about the number of characters that are going to be in Vengeance, I think we'll be getting La Capitan's nemesis, or more specifically, nemeses in Vengeance. I strongly believe that La Capitan's nemesis will be a hero deck consisting of four distinct heroes that use one deck. Whether they share a hero character card or not, I don't know.

I got this theory from the fact that La Capitan's nemesis's icon has four distinct parts. Then, Christopher mentioned that the idea of 5 villain decks and 5 hero decks meaning there would be 10 characters in Vengeance was not the case. Since it wouldn't make sense for there to be less than 10 characters in 10 decks (excluding environments), this has to mean one of the decks has more than one character.

And since we know who the five villain decks will be, that only leaves at least one of the hero decks to contain more than one character. But I doubt they'd have more than one hero deck take the "multiple hero" approach, so I say one.

Just my theory. I'm open to further evidence or counter-arguments.

I'm not sure what to expect with Vengeance, and everytime I am very impressed with what comes out. However, I do feel that the Freedom...Number will be very different under the leadership of our Newest Legacy. By the time Vengeance takes place, Baron Blade (and the remaining members of the Freedom Gala) has been working the super-landscape for quite a while. A few have probably retired from full duty, the roster is changing, etc. Tachyon body cannot possibly hold up perfectly forever with the strain it goes through with her abilities. I would imagine that Tempest, being an alien, would probably stick around, and Wraith could pull a Dark Knight Returns thing. I've tossed the thought around of Visionary joining forces, but her story has finally met with some level of resolution. The timeline that she needed to stop has been stopped, and I'm unsure if she will retire to live it, or if we will meet the real Visionary now that she isn't completely focused on her necessary mission. I feel we are entering a new era of comics in the game. Issue numbers for a few of the newest villains are pretty high up there in the hundreds and I think the newest form of the Freedom W'ever will be the newer, younger generation with newer, younger nemeses. Kismet is a fine example of this, actually.

 

But then...time never works properly in the comic-verse, even for characters in the same universe. Tachyon may age only a few years while Newest Legacy gains a decade. Who's to say?

 

I see Vengeance continuing the tale of Legacy vs. Blade. Blade can finally finish the entire Parsons line and vindicating his family, and Pauline can put a stop to the Baron's schemes and put down the man that took away her father.
